answer_1.quote: Human tutoring is a cornerstone of educational development, playing a crucial role in fostering societal growth by empowering learners.
answer_1.outputs: tutor responses in educational dialogues aimed at remediating student mistakes in mathematics

answer_2.quote: General domain-agnostic natural language generation (NLG) metrics like BLEU, BERTScore, DialogRPT, and so on have been used as proxies to measure the coherence and human-likeness of AI tutor responses.

answer_3.quote: Due to the growing interest in utilizing LLMs as critics or evaluators, we also used two LLMs as evaluators: • We used Prometheus2 (Kim et al., 2024) because: (i) it was specifically trained as an evaluator using reinforcement learning with human feedback (RLHF), (ii) it has a high correlation with human annotations and GPT-4, and (iii) it does not belong to any of the LLM families considered as AI tutors in our framework. • In addition, we also used Llama-3.1-8B as a lightweight LLM to assess the reliability of smaller models that were not fine-tuned for evaluation objectives as a critic.
methods: LLM-based evaluation using prompt in Figure

answer_4.quote: Four trained annotators (see Section 4.2) annotated MRBench using the validated taxonomy.
answer_4.guideline: Each dimension was annotated using a three-tier labeling system (see Figure and Table 4). For instance, the 'mistake identification' dimension employed the following labels: (i) yes, (ii) to some extent, and (iii) no.
